title: The birds
hook: Francis preaches to the birds, who stay to listen

segments.voice: Yesterday, the wolf of Gubbio, and a peace where the town fed its old enemy. Your line was brother wolf. Did you catch yourself asking what something was hungry for? Day one thousand two hundred fourteen.

What would you say to a flock of birds, if you thought they were listening? Shoo, maybe. Francis is on the road with his companions in the Umbrian countryside when he sees trees by the way filled with birds, and more of them on the ground. He tells his brothers to wait for him on the road. Then he walks over, alone, into the middle of the birds. And they don't scatter. The ones in the trees come down. They gather around his feet and keep still, as if waiting. He has an audience. So he does what he always does with an audience. He preaches. Today, what a saint finds to say to the birds.
screen: `TREES FULL OF BIRDS.` → `THEY DON'T SCATTER.` → `SO HE PREACHES.`

segments.voice: The story is told by Thomas of Celano, an early biographer of Francis, and again in the Little Flowers. Francis begins the way he begins with anyone: my little sisters the birds. And his sermon is not a scolding. It's a list of gifts. You owe a great deal to God your Creator, he tells them, so praise him always. He gave you freedom to fly anywhere. He gave you clothing, feathers twice and three times over. He kept your kind safe in Noah's ark. He gave you the air to move in, springs and rivers to drink from, mountains and valleys for shelter, and tall trees to build your nests. And you don't sow or reap, and God feeds you anyway. That last line is Jesus's own, from the Sermon on the Mount, in the Douay-Rheims: "Behold the birds of the air, for they neither sow, nor do they reap, nor gather into barns." Francis is simply reading the gospel back to the ones it was about. Then the story slows down to watch the birds. The Little Flowers says they open their beaks, stretch out their necks, spread their wings, and bow their heads to the ground, as if to show they understood. They don't leave until he blesses them with the sign of the cross. Then they rise all at once, singing, and go off in four directions, north, south, east and west, so that the flock itself makes the shape of a cross in the sky. Celano adds a small, human detail afterward. Francis blamed himself for never having preached to birds before. From then on, the story says, he urged every creature he met to praise its Maker. For Francis, praise wasn't only a human job. In his eyes the whole creation was singing, and he'd been slow to join in.
screen: `MY LITTLE SISTERS THE BIRDS.` · `A SERMON THAT'S A LIST OF GIFTS.` · `THEY BOW, THEN FLY OFF IN A CROSS.` · `HE BLAMED HIMSELF FOR BEING LATE.` · then, large: `BEHOLD THE BIRDS OF THE AIR.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: stop and listen to birds. If you can, open a window or step outside. If not, sit where you are. Settle, and breathe. Now listen outward, past the hum of the house, past the traffic. Wait for a bird. It may take a while. When one comes, don't name the species or reach for your phone. Just hear it the way Francis heard his audience: something alive, making its own sound, not for you. If there are no birds today, listen for any living sound at all. If you pray, you can let that sound be a small praise you join. If you don't, simply let it be company. The bell holds the time.
The birds. The flock Francis called his little sisters, preached to about God's gifts, and blessed before they flew. Today's word.
Your line: sisters birds. Today, the next time a bird calls, stop for one breath and let it finish before you move on. Day one thousand two hundred fourteen.

howItsDone: Catholics remember Francis's sermon to the birds in art and story, and on or near his feast day some parishes hold a blessing of animals in his honor.

original.note: Italian, the language of the Little Flowers: birds.

trapdoor: what you thought: a gentle saint who liked animals.
what it means: a sermon to the birds about God's gifts, ending in a blessing and a flock flying off in a cross.
what a scholar hears: Celano's early account and the Little Flowers both tell it, and Francis reads Matthew 6:26 back to the birds it names.

notes: Sermon content paraphrased from the Fioretti ch. 16 (gifts: freedom to fly, double and triple clothing, Noah's ark, air, springs and rivers, mountains and valleys, trees for nests, food without sowing or reaping; bowing; the blessing; flying in four directions in a cross). Confirm the details and their order.

Celano detail (Francis reproaching himself for negligence in not preaching to birds before, then exhorting all creatures to praise): confirm the reference, usually given as 1 Celano 58 / Book 1 ch. 21.
The location is kept general ('the Umbrian countryside'); tradition places it near Bevagna / Cannara.
